doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Father's love of all music and his jazz listening
summary: His father loved gospel and jazz alike, told him about Fletcher Henderson, Ellington and Basie, and they listened to records and radio together.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I want to go back a little bit. Let’s say you were 13 or so, 1953, and your family was very into Gospel music. If you had brought home a record by Louis Jordan or some of the, you know the blues guys, would that have been accepted in your household?

Oh that’s why I was really blessed man, actually I’ve got two younger brothers who were very challenging. And my father played the four string guitar and he had a beautiful tenor voice. My two younger brothers got that tenor voice. But he loved music. He told me they would perform at the Apollo Theater and he would go, after that he would go listen to all the jazz groups, and he’d come back home and tell me about them and we’d go down in the basement and we’d listen to records, or back then you know the radio was the main thing. And so it was interesting you know because I loved Duke Ellington and Count Basie, but he knew all about Fletcher Henderson. I didn’t know anything about Fletcher Henderson. And he would tell me, say yeah, you’ve got to listen to him because you know people overlooked him. And so I was really blessed. My father, he just loved all music.
